dimensions.assessment: Directly affects Department of State personnel performing consular functions, specifically those on limited non-career appointments.
dimensions.evidence: Expanding limited non-career appointments for Department of State personnel performing consular functions, including through the Consular Fellows Program

dimensions.assessment: Provides administrative flexibility to extend employment terms for consular personnel up to ten years total, impacting their career duration.
dimensions.evidence: To authorize the Secretary of State to extend limited consular appointments to eight years, with an additional two-year extension for needs of the Foreign Service.

dimensions.assessment: Aims to reduce recruitment costs and delays, but does not appropriate specific new federal spending amounts.
dimensions.evidence: increasing staffing capacity, reducing recruitment costs and delays, and ensuring the continued efficient delivery of consular services.

dimensions.assessment: Amends a specific section (Section 309) of the Foreign Service Act of 1980 regarding limited consular appointments.
dimensions.evidence: Section 309 of the Foreign Service Act of 1980 (22 U.S.C. 3949) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Permanently amends the Foreign Service Act to alter the allowable duration of limited consular appointments.
dimensions.evidence: Section 309 of the Foreign Service Act of 1980 (22 U.S.C. 3949) is amended

importance_detail.rationale: The bill authorizes the Secretary of State to extend limited consular appointments from five years to eight years, plus an additional two-year extension, directly affecting Department of State personnel performing consular services.
